strengths: The paper addresses a well-motivated problem with an identifiable audience: identifying approximately Pareto-optimal designs under noisy, expensive evaluations over continuous spaces.

Adaptive partitioning, confidence rectangles covering entire cells, and explicit discarding and covering rules form a coherent algorithmic approach. Considering dependent objectives and both information-based and dimension-based complexity bounds provides useful perspectives.

The manuscript includes explanatory figures, pseudocode, and detailed proofs. Experiments use 10 sampled functions with five runs each, include qNEHVI, and report an informative trade-off between tree depth, accuracy, and runtime.
weaknesses: Necessary: Theorem 1's stated guarantee needs a corrected proof. V_h contains log(h²) despite being defined for h ≥ 0, leaving the root parameter undefined. In Corollary 1, substituting the chosen u into Lemma 7 produces 2h log N, whereas V_h contains only h log N. Lemma 14, equation (31), also assumes that the parent's refinement inequality remains valid at a later time, although β increases. These steps do not establish the advertised confidence calibration and dimension bound. Correct the parameters and explicitly track refinement-time bounds or inherited rectangles.

Necessary: Proposition 1 and Appendix C do not establish linear information gain under the stated assumptions. The final lower bound is T multiplied by a factor involving amplitudes a_Tj that may tend to zero; this does not imply Ω(T). Keeping the relevant amplitudes bounded away from zero creates infinitely many designs separated in the GP metric, conflicting with compactness and the Hölder condition. Merely asserting that a suitable metric exists does not resolve this. Supply a valid example satisfying all assumptions or remove the claimed separation supported by this proposition.

Necessary: The experimental accuracy definitions are inconsistent with the theoretical target. Section 7.1 checks whether a predicted point is ε-dominated by a true Pareto point, which also accepts arbitrarily poor dominated predictions. This is not membership in Z_ε(X). The coverage description also treats ε-domination and 2ε-domination as equivalent. Provide exact indicators consistent with Definitions 3–5 and recompute results if needed. Report accuracy and coverage separately instead of only their average in Table 2; average pointwise scores do not establish the probability that an entire returned set satisfies the guarantee.

Necessary: Clarify the empirical protocol and qualify the performance conclusions. The manuscript does not sufficiently specify how returned continuous cells become finite predicted fronts, how baseline fronts are extracted, or how confidence intervals account for repeated runs on the same function. The fast depth-9/10 variants set V_h to zero and therefore lose the theorem's control of variation within cells; this limitation should be explicit. The theoretical depth-24 configuration takes 15:15:24, versus 40 seconds for qNEHVI. Conclusions should distinguish evaluation efficiency, runtime, and guarantees, and remain limited to the tested one-dimensional, independent-objective setting.

Optional: A controlled comparison with uniform discretization would help isolate the benefit of adaptation. Correlated-objective and higher-dimensional experiments would broaden the empirical findings, but are not prerequisites if the claims are appropriately scoped.

strengths: The paper addresses a useful problem with an identifiable audience in Bayesian optimization and Pareto active learning: certifying an approximate Pareto set over a continuous design space.

Combining regional GP confidence rectangles, inherited bounds, and adaptive refinement is a coherent algorithmic approach. The phase-by-phase explanation, illustrations, and pseudocode make the main ideas accessible.
The multi-output formulation accommodates dependent objectives, and investigating sample complexity through both information gain and metric dimension offers a useful theoretical perspective.

The experiments include 10 sampled functions with five runs each, larger evaluation budgets for competitors, and a tree-depth ablation. The full-depth method achieves the lowest reported MSE and strong performance at stringent accuracy thresholds in the tested setting.
weaknesses: Necessary: The high-probability guarantee needs a corrected derivation. In Theorem 1 and Corollary 1, V_h contains log(h²) although h starts at zero. Furthermore, substituting the chosen u into Lemma 7 produces 2h log N, whereas the stated V_h contains only h log N. These inconsistencies affect the uniform confidence event supporting correctness. Separately, Lemma 14, equation (31), applies the parent's refinement inequality at a later evaluation count; the increasing confidence multiplier means this inequality does not automatically persist. Inherited rectangles may provide a repair, but the supplied argument does not establish it. Corrections must be propagated through the theorem and its parameter choices.

Necessary: Proposition 1 does not establish the claimed linear information gain. Appendix C derives a lower bound T times a coefficient depending on the amplitudes at index T, then treats that coefficient as a positive constant independent of T. The amplitudes may converge to zero. Conversely, maintaining nonvanishing variances at infinitely many independent locations creates a uniformly separated sequence in the GP metric, incompatible with compactness and the Hölder metric condition in Assumption 1. The unspecified 'suitably chosen metric' does not resolve this. A valid example or a narrower claim is needed before concluding that the two bounds have the advertised separation.

Necessary: The experimental accuracy definitions are inconsistent with the formal guarantee. Section 7.1 says accuracy checks whether a predicted point is epsilon-dominated by a true Pareto point. Under Definition 1, this also accepts arbitrarily poor dominated points; it does not test membership in the epsilon-Pareto front. For example, with true front {(1,1)}, prediction (0,0) passes that domination test for epsilon = 0.05 but lies outside the required band. Coverage also alternates between epsilon and 2epsilon as though they were equivalent. Provide precise operational formulas, explain how returned regions are converted into evaluated points, and correct results if the implementation follows these descriptions. Report accuracy and coverage separately rather than only their average.

Necessary: The practical conclusions should distinguish the tested tradeoffs and the scope of the guarantee. Setting V_h = 0 at a truncated depth removes the bound on variation inside cells, so Theorem 1 does not certify those faster variants. The full-depth run takes about 15 hours, while qNEHVI takes 40 seconds; the 27-second truncated variant has worse MSE and worse performance at the strictest threshold than qNEHVI. These results support a tradeoff within the one-dimensional, independent-objective setting, rather than a general simultaneous speed and accuracy advantage.

Optional: Experiments with correlated objectives, higher-dimensional inputs, and a controlled fixed-grid ablation would clarify practical applicability and isolate the benefit of adaptive discretization. These extensions are not prerequisites if the empirical claims are appropriately scoped; the unresolved proof and metric issues are the reasons for leaning reject.

Regional confidence rectangles, inheritance of cumulative uncertainty sets, and the refinement-versus-evaluation rule provide a coherent approach to extending finite-design Pareto active learning.

weaknesses: Necessary: Proposition 1 and Appendix C do not establish the claimed linear information gain. The final lower bound is T multiplied by a quantity involving a_Tj²/(a_Tj²+σ²), which can vanish with T. Keeping the relevant amplitudes bounded away from zero creates infinitely many independent, separated GP values, incompatible with the Hölder condition on a compact metric space. The assertion that a suitable metric exists does not resolve this. Provide a valid comparison of the two complexity bounds or withdraw this proposition and its claimed demonstration of their non-dominance.

Necessary: The confidence calibration underlying Theorem 1 needs correction. V_h is defined for h ≥ 0 using log(h²), making the root value undefined. Furthermore, substituting the stated u into Lemma 7 produces a 2h log N contribution, whereas Corollary 1 includes h log N. Re-derive the uniform variation event and specify root conventions. Algorithm 1 also computes the pessimistic Pareto set before constructing the current R_t rectangles on which its definition depends; its ordering must match the analysis.

Necessary: Lemma 14, particularly equations (31) and (33), applies the parent's refinement inequality at the current round. That inequality was established when the parent was refined. Because β grows, decreasing posterior variance alone does not preserve the inequality at later rounds. Inheritance of cumulative rectangles may permit a repair, but the manuscript must supply that argument and verify the resulting dimension bound.

Necessary: The experimental metrics are inconsistent with the formal accuracy criterion. In Section 7.1, checking whether a prediction is ε-dominated by a true Pareto point accepts arbitrarily poor predictions; this does not establish membership in Z_ε. Coverage also alternates between ε and 2ε, which are not equivalent. State the actual formulas, explain how returned cell unions are evaluated, and recompute affected results. Report accuracy and coverage separately instead of only their average in Table 2. High average ratios also do not establish the claimed probability that an entire returned set is ε-accurate.

Necessary: Restrict the empirical superiority and efficiency claims to the demonstrated setting, or provide additional supporting evidence. Experiments cover only one-dimensional inputs with two independent squared-exponential objectives. The theoretical-depth run takes over fifteen hours, while the fast truncated variants set V_h to zero despite nonzero within-cell variation. Those variants therefore do not inherit the stated regional confidence guarantee and should be explicitly identified as heuristic approximations.

Optional: A matched fixed-grid PAL ablation, evaluation-budget curves, and experiments with correlated objectives or larger input dimension would clarify when adaptivity and objective dependence help.
